title: fix: validate text streams before splitting for billing
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes the #14494 gap by validating before the existing client/billing stream split.
- Simplifies Chat validation: retain the latest non-null usage and validate at DONE, allowing provisional early counts. Removes 11 runtime lines; no new abstractions.
- Keeps explicit-error detection, failed-stream no-charge behavior, and Responses terminal validation.
- Covers successful final-usage wallet charges, invalid-final-usage no-charge behavior, provider costs, null usage, and SSE framing. 213 focused tests passed with an isolated snapshot server; a default-setup rerun hit an existing non-stream Perplexity timeout. Type-checking and Biome pass.

gist.headline: Count the nectar twice
gist.blurb: The billing stream now checks its pollen before splitting into client and wallet paths. A malformed final usage report no longer gets to buzz past the gate.
gist.summary: Text streaming now validates final usage data before the client/billing stream split, retaining the latest non-null provisional count until DONE and charging wallets only for valid successful streams.
gist.impact: Users get reliable final-usage wallet charges while streams with invalid final usage, explicit errors, or failed completions remain uncharged; Responses streams keep their terminal validation too.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy stream-splitting garden irrigation gate: incoming glowing API droplets pass through a careful usage-check meter before flowing into two channels, one toward a friendly client terminal and one toward a pollen wallet jar. Polli, wearing tiny accountant glasses and holding a clipboard, inspects the final droplet while a code-plant grows beside the validated channel; malformed droplets are gently redirected into a harmless compost tray.
